title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}. It is free profinite on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ subject to one relation; the images below are consistent with l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. Ŝ^+_{0,3} is the profinite group generated by an involution σ_∞ and an element ρ of order 3. It contains Π̂_{0,3}, and ε_0 = σ_∞ρ satisfies ε_0^2 = l_0. It is the orbifold fundamental group of (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3, i.e. the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. The symbol u is an element of a GT-type group acting on Π̂_{0,3} by u(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^p), u(l_1) = int(g_1)(l_1^p), with p the cyclotomic-type exponent and g_1 = σ_∞(g_0). Relation (17) on the previous page, flagged '?', proposes the extension u(ε_0) = int(g_0)(ε_0^p) to Ŝ^+.

This page. Grothendieck considers a second homomorphism (18), φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3}, with l_0 ↦ ε_0 = σ_∞ρ, l_1 ↦ σ_∞, l_∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}.
- The product relation checks: ρ^{-1}σ_∞σ_∞ρ = 1.
- φ̂ is surjective; its kernel is the normal closure of l_1^2 and l_∞^3.
- Geometrically it is the orbifold map from the thrice-punctured line onto the j-line, with orbifold points of orders 2 and 3 and a cusp. That is, it is the Belyi/j-map picture of PSL_2(Z)^.

He demands that φ̂ commute with u up to an inner automorphism. So there is λ ∈ Ŝ^+ with φ̂(u x) = λ u(φ̂ x) λ^{-1} for all x (formula 20). It suffices to check this on the generators l_0 and l_1.

For x = l_0, since φ̂(u l_0) = int(φ̂(g_0))(ε_0^p), one gets (21): u(ε_0) = int(λ^{-1} φ̂(g_0))(ε_0^p). Comparing with (17), g_0^{-1} λ^{-1} φ̂(g_0) centralizes ε_0^p. Using that the centralizer of ε_0 is the procyclic group ε_0^{Ẑ} (a hypothesis already voiced on the previous page), he gets g_0^{-1} λ^{-1} φ̂(g_0) = ε_0^β with β ∈ Ẑ. This gives the boxed formula (22): λ = φ̂(g_0) ε_0^{-β} g_0^{-1}.

A marginal addition rewrites λ as φ̂ of something, roughly φ̂(σ_∞(g_0)), referring to (24 bis). The page ends by starting the case x = l_1. The next page turns that case into the boxed constraint (24): ε_1^{-β} h_0 ε_0^β = σ_∞(φ̂(h_0))^{-1} φ̂(h_0), with h_0 = [σ_∞, g_0].

Purpose. Note that existence of λ is automatic: u sends l_1 and l_∞ to conjugates of their p-th powers, so it preserves the kernel of φ̂. The real content is to make λ explicit. One then extracts from the compatibility of u with the S_3/PSL_2(Z)^ structure functional equations on the 'lacet' g_0. These are the analogues of the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, i.e. GT acting on profinite PSL_2(Z) / B_3 / M_{1,1}. An integer-like invariant β appears; the next page's margin observes that β is determined only modulo 2 under changes of g_0.
errors: The step from (21) and (17) to g_0^{-1}λ^{-1}φ̂(g_0) ∈ ε_0^{Ẑ} relies on (17), which is itself marked '?' on the previous page. It also relies on the centralizer of ε_0 (equivalently of ε_0^p, p a unit) in Ŝ^+_{0,3} being ε_0^{Ẑ}. That holds in Z/2*Z/3 and is true profinitely by results on centralizers in free profinite products, but it is not proved on the page.

Existence of λ is not an extra condition: it follows because u maps l_1 and l_∞ to conjugates of l_1^p and l_∞^p, so u preserves ker φ̂. The page phrases it as a condition ('écrivons qu'il commute'). The substantive output is the explicit form of λ, not its existence.
The marginal identification λ = φ̂(g_0 l_0^{-1}) or φ̂(σ_∞(g_0)) is only asserted with a forward reference '(24 bis)'. Its exponents (β versus a fixed value) are not justified on this page.

ideas.what: The surjection Π̂_{0,3} → (Z/2*Z/3)^, l_0 ↦ σ_∞ρ, l_1 ↦ σ_∞, l_∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}. This is the orbifold j-map from P^1−{0,1,∞} to the moduli orbifold of elliptic curves (profinite PSL_2(Z)).
ideas.modern_name: π_1 of the j-line orbifold / profinite PSL_2(Z) as a quotient of F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (modular group); in the GT context Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Harbater–Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1}, SL_2(Z) and dessins, but not this explicit compatibility computation

ideas.what: Requiring a GT-type automorphism u of Π̂_{0,3} to be compatible, up to inner automorphism, with the S_3-orbifold quotient (Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL_2(Z)^). The aim is to extract explicit equations on the conjugating 'lacet' g_0; λ is determined explicitly as φ̂(g_0) ε_0^{-β} g_0^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT (or of Gal(Q̄/Q)) on profinite PSL_2(Z) / B_3; derivation of the GT 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations from S_3-symmetry

ideas.what: Introduction of an auxiliary invariant β ∈ Ẑ, the centralizer exponent. The next page shows it changes by even amounts under g_0 ↦ g_0 ε_0^λ, so only its parity is intrinsic.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization ambiguity of the conjugating element in an outer action (centralizer twist)

missed.claim: In unpublished notes continuing La Longue Marche, Grothendieck explicitly computes how a GT-type outer automorphism of Π̂_{0,3} descends to the orbifold group (Z/2*Z/3)^ through the j-type map φ̂. He derives the conjugator λ = φ̂(g_0) ε_0^{-β} g_0^{-1}, leading on the next page to a commutator constraint on g_0. This is an independent, pre-Drinfeld/Ihara derivation of GT-type symmetry relations via PSL_2(Z)^. Its general spirit is known (Esquisse), but these explicit formulas are not.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents how close Grothendieck came to the explicit defining relations of GT, by a route through profinite PSL_2(Z) rather than braid groups. Mathematically the result is subsumed by later GT theory.

missed.claim: The status of the extension (17) of u to ε_0, and of the residual parameter β, is left open: β is only determined mod 2 (next page), and this page also uses an unproved centralizer property. Grothendieck suggests reducing to β ∈ {0,1} and treating it as a 'fundamental' number. This is not pursued here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: a parity-type invariant attached to the lift of GT elements to the S_3-extended group. It is likely trivializable by normalization in the modern treatment, but this would need checking.

deep.surprise_reason: Explicit, careful computation of GT-type relations through compatibility with the S_3/PSL_2(Z)^ orbifold quotient, predating the published GT literature. The underlying ideas (GT, the action on PSL_2(Z)^) are now standard and were partly signposted in Esquisse, so this is a notable historical detail rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read roughly 'Considérons maintenant l'hom. (13)'; the source of φ̂ is Π̂_{0,3} (with hat), not 'Π̂_{03}'.
The garbled 'avec u [?] près à un [?] automorphisme intérieur près [?], à u' should read roughly 'et écrivons qu'il commute, à automorphisme intérieur près, à u'.
The exponent in (21) and in the following line is most likely p (the exponent of (11)/(17) on the previous page), not ρ: read l'_0^{p}.
The label '(23)' before 'g_0^{-1}λ^{-1}φ̂(g_0) = l'^β_0' is crossed out on the original.
The target group is written as a script S/G with hat and +, Ŝ^+_{0,3}; the next page's transcription renders the same symbol as Ĝ^+_{03}.
The marginal addition after box (22) reads approximately '= φ̂(g_0 l_0^{-1}) = φ̂(σ_∞(g_0)) cf plus bas (24 bis)'. Its exponent is uncertain in the image.
